arxiv-2208-03297.title: Counter-flow induced clustering: Exact results
arxiv-2208-03297.creator: Amit Kumar Chatterjee, Hisao Hayakawa
arxiv-2208-03297.description: Abstract We analyze the cluster formation in a non-ergodic stochastic system as a result of counter-flow, with the aid of an exactly solvable model. To illustrate the clustering, a two species asymmetric simple exclusion process with impurities on a periodic lattice is considered, where the impurity can activate flips between the two non-conserved species.

arxiv-2309-09000.title: The Quantum-Extended Church-Turing Thesis in Quantum Field Theory
arxiv-2309-09000.creator: Cameron Cianci
arxiv-2309-09000.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Cameron Cianci. The quantum-Extended Church-Turing thesis has been explored in many physical theories including general relativity but lacks exploration in quantum field theories such as quantum electrodynamics. Through construction of a computational model whose gate set mimics the interactions of QED, we demonstrate that one of the defining features of quantum field theory, particle creation and annihilation, is not likely to violate the quantum-Extended Church-Turing thesis. Through this computational model, it is shown that particle creation is likely only another form of quantum parallelism.

arxiv-2408-11898.title: Non-Clifford diagonalization for measurement shot reduction in quantum expectation value estimation
arxiv-2408-11898.creator: Nicolas PD Sawaya, Daan Camps, Norm M Tubman, Grant M Rotskoff, Ryan LaRose
arxiv-2408-11898.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nicolas PD Sawaya, Daan Camps, Norm M Tubman, Grant M Rotskoff, Ryan LaRose. Estimating expectation values on near-term quantum computers often requires a prohibitively large number of measurements. One widely-used strategy to mitigate this problem has been to partition an operator’s Pauli terms into sets of mutually commuting operators. Here, we introduce a method that relaxes this constraint of commutativity, instead allowing for entirely arbitrary terms to be grouped together, save a locality constraint.

arxiv-2411-09888.title: Quantum-Inspired Stochastic Modeling and Regularity Analysis in Turbulent Flows
arxiv-2411-09888.creator: Rômulo Damasclin Chaves dos Santos, Jorge Henrique de Oliveira Sales
arxiv-2411-09888.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel mathematical framework for examining the regularity and energy dissipation properties of solutions to the stochastic Navier-Stokes equations. By integrating Sobolev-Besov hybrid spaces, fractional differential operators, and quantum-inspired modeling techniques, we provide a comprehensive analysis that captures the multiscale and chaotic dynamics inherent in turbulent flows.

arxiv-2412-10360.title: Apollo: An Exploration of Video Understanding in Large Multimodal Models
arxiv-2412-10360.creator: Orr Zohar, Xiaohan Wang, Yann Dubois, Nikhil Mehta, Tong Xiao, Philippe Hansen-Estruch, Licheng Yu, Xiaofang Wang, Felix Juefei-Xu, Ning Zhang, Serena Yeung-Levy, Xide Xia
arxiv-2412-10360.description: Abstract Despite the rapid integration of video perception capabilities into Large Multimodal Models (LMMs), the underlying mechanisms driving their video understanding remain poorly understood. Consequently, many design decisions in this domain are made without proper justification or analysis. The high computational cost of training and evaluating such models, coupled with limited open research, hinders the development of video-LMMs.

arxiv-2503-03002.title: Multi-Step Deep Koopman Network (MDK-Net) for Vehicle Control in Frenet Frame
arxiv-2503-03002.creator: Mohammad Abtahi, Mahdis Rabbani, Armin Abdolmohammadi, Shima Nazari
arxiv-2503-03002.description: Abstract The highly nonlinear dynamics of vehicles present a major challenge for the practical implementation of optimal and Model Predictive Control (MPC) approaches in path planning and following. Koopman operator theory offers a global linear representation of nonlinear dynamical systems, making it a promising framework for optimization-based vehicle control.

arxiv-2508-00817.title: String-based axial and helicity-flip GPDs: a comparison to lattice QCD
arxiv-2508-00817.creator: Florian Hechenberger, Kiminad A. Mamo, Ismail Zahed
arxiv-2508-00817.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Florian Hechenberger, Kiminad A. Mamo, Ismail Zahed. We construct an analytic, string - based representation of the nucleon’s axial and helicity - flip conformal moments of generalized parton distributions that holds for any skewness and for both the quark and gluon channels. The starting point is the Mellin–Barnes resummation of the conformal partial wave expansion, where the moments are parametrized by open - (Reggeon) and closed - string (Pomeron) trajectories with slopes determined by experimental form factors and meson/glueball spectroscopy.

pmc-12822296.title: Curcumin induces ferroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma by regulating the P62-KEAP1-NRF2-signaling pathway
pmc-12822296.creator: Jinlan Deng, Zhijuan Wu, Shangkun Ning, Xu Chang, Jibing Liu, Yangli Yu, Min Zhang, Lin Zhang
pmc-12822296.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Context Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a major global health challenge, with limited treatment options owing to chemotherapy resistance and severe systemic toxicity. Curcumin demonstrates broad-spectrum antitumor activity against HCC and various other malignancies. Ferroptosis, a regulated form of cell death driven by iron overload, glutathione depletion, and lipid peroxidation, has recently gained attention as a potential therapeutic strategy in cancer treatment.

pmc-13079486.title: Membrane Biofouling: Current Understanding and Future Perspectives- An Overview
pmc-13079486.creator: N. Phillip, A. A. Muleja, M. M. Motsa, B. B. Mamba, T. T. I. Nkambule, C. S. Tshangana
pmc-13079486.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Membrane technology is a compelling alternative for addressing some water quality issues on a global scale. Despite the demonstrated success of membrane technology, biofouling remains a persistent problem in membrane filtration processes. The impact of biofouling compromises the application and efficiency of the filtration processes by shortening membrane lifespan, reducing permeate output, increasing the energy requirements, and increasing the transmembrane pressure. All these factors combined impact treatment plant operations.

pmc-13179885.title: Should checkpoint inhibitors be reserved for biomarker-selected pediatric brain tumors?
pmc-13179885.creator: Yaxel Levin-Carrion, Jayant Bhasin, Kevin Titkov, Sraavya Anne, Arman Sawhney, Caryn J. Ha, Ibraheem Sharaf, Marvens Jean, Jacob Santana, Drew Thibault, Alejandro Pando, Nemanja Novakovic, Nehal S. Parikh, Morana Vojnic, Jonathan H. Sherman
pmc-13179885.description: PurposePediatric brain tumors, including high-grade gliomas (HHG), medulloblastomas (MB), and ependymomas (EPN), are a leading cause of death in children. They are often immunologically “cold” with low tumor mutational burden (TMB) and very few tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), which may limit the role of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI).

pmc-13473844.creator: Jonathan A. Salazar, Shira Rockowitz, Courtney E. French, Wanqing Shao, Daniel M. Elman, Alexandra N. Carey, Tom Jaksic, Piotr Sliz, Wen Hann Tan, Christopher P. Duggan

pmc-13539056.creator: Mithen Ravisankar, Muniza Bai, Vignesh Kumar Kathiresan, Jefferson Daniel Jawahar, Balamugesh Thangakunam, Angel Miraclin Thirugnanakumar, Elanthenral Sigamani
pmc-13539056.description: An immunocompetent young male in his early 20s presented with a 1‐month history of central chest pain, dyspepsia and significant weight loss. Initial evaluation revealed a large, deep oesophageal ulcer and extensive necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Endobronchial ultrasound‐guided fine‐needle aspiration of the mediastinal nodes confirmed necrotising granulomatous inflammation, suggestive of tuberculosis.

pmc-13612854.creator: Hossein Fadaei, Mehraban Shahmari, Reza Nemati‐Vakilabad, Fateme Ebrahimi Belil
pmc-13612854.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Aim(s)Currently, no valid and reliable instrument exists in Persian to assess intensive care unit (ICU) nurses' self‐efficacy in delirium care, which limits the ability to identify educational needs and evaluate targeted interventions in Iranian critical care settings. This study aimed to evaluate the psychometric properties of the Persian version of the Delirium Care Self‐Efficacy Scale (P‐DCSE‐I) for ICU nurses in Iran.DesignA methodological study with a cross‐sectional design.MethodsThe original scale was translated into Persian using a forward‐backward method.

pmc-13639505.title: Decoverslipping of Archival Cytology Aspirate Smears for Ancillary Studies: A Review of Methods and Institutional Experience With Freezer‐Based Techniques

pmc-13639505.description: IntroductionArchival cytology aspirate smears are increasingly used for ancillary testing, yet decoverslipping remains a practical bottleneck.
